name: Shallum
overview: Shallum was a male Levite known as a singer who had married a foreign wife, as recorded in Ezra 10:24. He belonged to the tribe of Levi, which was set apart for service in the temple. The mention of his foreign marriage highlights a specific issue addressed in the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Shallum means 'peace, well-being, prosperity' in Hebrew. This proper name reflects positive qualities but was not given directly by God. It is the only name recorded for this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Shallum is identified explicitly as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe. Scripture does not provide further details on his family beyond his marriage to a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Shallum's significance lies in his role as a Levite singer who was involved in the issue of intermarriage with foreign women during the post-exilic period. His mention in Ezra 10:24 underscores the community's efforts to maintain covenantal purity and obedience to God's commands. Through Shallum, the text highlights the challenges faced by returned exiles in preserving their identity and faithfulness to the Lord.
